conventions.convention: The mode count r is a positive finite integer; the action scale ℏ is positive. Finite-mode bosonic Fock space remains infinite-dimensional, with occupation indices starting at zero.

Inner products are linear in the first argument. Quadratures are Q_j=√ℏ x_j and P_j=−i√ℏ ∂_j after the specified Fock–Schrödinger identification, with maximal multiplication and Fourier-multiplier domains.
The default quadrature order is interleaved, R=(Q₁,P₁,…,Qᵣ,Pᵣ), with J the direct sum of blocks [[0,1],[-1,0]]. Grouped coordinates use the explicitly specified permutation and J₀=[[0,I],[-I,0]].
Weyl labels satisfy W(z)W(z′)=exp(−iℏ zᵀJz′/2)W(z+z′). Quadrature covariance M*RM=SR corresponds to label covariance M*W(z)M=W(Sᵀz).
The imported Fourier transform uses exp(−2πix·ξ); the angular-frequency unitary is (2π)^(−r/2) times that transform evaluated at k/(2π).

Finite density-operator moments are weighted quadrature forms in a positive-eigenvalue spectral expansion; covariance takes the real part of the centered cross form. The uncertainty inequality is V+iℏJ/2 ⪰ 0.

Normalized quadratic propagators have entrywise integrable real symmetric coefficients, no linear or scalar Hamiltonian term, and Schwartz trajectories absolutely continuous in every seminorm. Their endpoint phases differ only by sign; arbitrary individual Weyl implementers retain arbitrary scalar phase.
The squeeze dilation is U_s f(x)=e^(−s/2)f(e^(−s)x), so U_s*QU_s=e^sQ and U_s*PU_s=e^(−s)P.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, r≥1 and ℏ>0, defines the self-adjoint finite-mode quadratures, common transported Schwartz domain, regular irreducible Weyl system, finite density-operator second moments, mean, covariance and Gaussian characteristic function.

Assume Countable Choice, r≥1 and ℏ>0. The occupation and product Hermite families are complete orthonormal families, and the map sending each occupation vector to its product Hermite function extends uniquely to a unitary from bosonic Fock space over C^r to L²(R^r), with the stated ladder and quadrature identities on the finite-particle span.

Every real finite symplectic matrix is a finite product of symmetric upper and lower shears, invertible coordinate changes and their inverses. Partial Fourier rotations are also such products; for every S there is such a product G for which the upper-left block of SG is invertible.

For the stated integrable real symmetric homogeneous quadratic Hamiltonians and normalized unitary Schwartz propagators, two classical paths with the same endpoint having invertible upper-right block give endpoint propagators U₂(T)=U₁(T) or U₂(T)=−U₁(T).

Assume AC, r≥1 and ℏ>0. Every finite real symplectic S has an individual unitary implementer with M_S*W(z)M_S=W(Sᵀz), unique up to scalar phase. The specified normalized homogeneous quadratic propagator endpoints form a connected topological group whose map to the symplectic group is a two-fold covering homomorphism with kernel {I,−I}.

Assume AC and the finite-mode conventions. If UU*−VV*=I and UVᵀ=VUᵀ, the stated real grouped matrix is symplectic and a unitary implements a′=Ua+Va* on the transported Schwartz core, with the stated Weyl covariance and mean number tr(VV*) in its transformed vacuum.

Assume Countable Choice, r≥1 and ℏ>0. Schwartz space is dense in the joint position and weak-derivative domain for the norm ||f||₂+Σ_j(||x_jf||₂+||∂_jf||₂); these weak-derivative domains agree with the Fourier-defined momentum domains.
Every real symmetric positive definite 2r×2r matrix V admits V=SDSᵀ with S interleaved symplectic and D=diag(ν₁,ν₁,…,νᵣ,νᵣ), ν_j>0. Moreover V+iℏJ/2 ⪰ 0 if and only if every ν_j≥ℏ/2.

Under AC and the finite-mode conventions, every density operator with finite quadrature second moments satisfies V+iℏJ/2 ⪰ 0; symplectic conjugation sends d,V to Sd,SVSᵀ and χ(z) to χ(Sᵀz). For every real d and real symmetric V, exp(izᵀd−zᵀVz/2) is a density-operator Weyl characteristic function if and only if V+iℏJ/2 ⪰ 0.

seams_checked.note: The metaplectic theorem uses thm-nrqmx-finite-weyl-uniqueness-interface with AC, nonzero Hilbert space, finite phase space, fixed nonzero parameter ℏ, regularity and irreducibility retained. The supplier states precisely this representation-equivalence interface; no infinite-mode conclusion is imported.

Opened the finite-mode assignment, beam-splitter theorem and loss-channel theorem. Their uses retain finite mode count, full Fock space, AC and occupation/core conventions. The beam-splitter proof explicitly converts M*aM=Ca to the state-action creator matrix Cᵀ, fixes the vacuum phase and proves finite-particle invariance. The mode diagram agrees with that assignment. Physical conclusions remain conditional ideal-model deductions.

Opened def-qsmx-finite-boson-quadratic-form and thm-qsmx-finite-boson-stability. They preserve grouped quadrature order, ℏ normalization, the exact Bogoliubov identities and Schwartz-preserving implementation. Stability explicitly assumes its diagonalization certificate and uses S_gᵀGS_g=D_ω in the correct conjugation direction; it asserts neither an infinite-mode result nor an unprovided certificate-existence theorem.
